target_customer: Warehouses and shippers that schedule inbound and outbound truck appointments
problem: Warehouses coordinate truck arrivals by phone and spreadsheet, causing driver wait times and dock congestion.
business_model: B2B SaaS dock scheduling and driver check-in (pricing not found)

founders.name: Andrew Denta
founders.background_notes: Named CEO in the Houston InnovationMap acquisition report; one summary says the founders were former Uber Freight staff and consultants but that is unverified. Some sources spell it Dent.

founders.name: Chris Podlaski
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no bio.

competitors.name: Opendock
competitors.traction_then: used by carriers and brokers such as C.H. Robinson, Schneider and Werner per a fall 2020 event page

technical_complexity.rationale: Scheduling, PO validation and text-based driver check-in are standard web and messaging features for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Several scheduling vendors existed and no data or network effects are documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Velostics, a dock and yard management firm, acquired Terusama in August 2021 and folded it into its platform.

market_need_then: A FreightWaves piece in April 2020 covered dock scheduling cutting driver wait times, showing visible demand.

branding.domain_note: The YC listing now points to velostics.com; the original terusama domain was not checked.

rebrands.why: Product was integrated into the acquirer's platform

brand_strength.rationale: An unusual invented name with no found brand coverage, absorbed into Velostics within about 18 months of the batch.

outcome_analysis: Terusama was a two person Winter 2020 team building dock scheduling and driver check-in for warehouses. Velostics acquired it in August 2021, about a year after founding, to add truck scheduling to its yard and load products, with terms undisclosed. The only funding found is a 150 thousand dollar aggregator figure, so this reads as a small, quick acquisition, probably a team and product tuck-in, but the price and motives are not public.
notes: A 150 thousand dollar seed from Y Combinator appears on Employbl and in the InnovationMap article citing Crunchbase; both rely on aggregator data, so no round is recorded. The Opendock source is a Loadsmart blog from June 2020, found through search result listing and not opened. Founder education and employers not found. The velostics.com homepage does not mention Terusama.
